correctness.rationale: Endpoint midpoint E and odd half-difference O are orthogonal, giving radius lower bound S. Setting x=t²/a², for even d and a²<=1 the coordinatewise bound (1−x^j)^2 <= 1−x^(2j−1) proves every curve point within ball centered E, and strictness aside from the stated contacts. For even d and a²>1, exact identity R²−||γ(t)−λE||²=Σ a^(4j) x^j(1+1/M−x^j−x^(j−1)/M) proves strict containment for 0<x<1, while λE is the strictly positive barycenter of 0 and two endpoints at equal radius, proving uniqueness/minimality. For odd d, pairing even terms with preceding or following odd terms (depending M<=1 or M>=1) bounds distance by S strictly except at |t|=a. Strict convexity excludes all other hull contacts. Fresh independent rational coordinate-norm checks (2460 distances) corroborate equations; they are not the unrestricted proof.

value.rationale: A sharp dimension-parity and real-scale contact transition for the canonical metric realization of cyclic polytopes, with a closed minimum-ball center/radius valid under arbitrarily many interior insertions. The two-vs-three support-point phenomenon is a concrete structural result useful for computational convex geometry and metric polytope comparisons.
residual_risks: Fixed unweighted monomial embedding is essential; nonorthogonal affine transforms do not preserve minimum ball.

final_claim: For all d>=2,a>0, compact T⊂[-a,a] containing −a,0,a, Euclidean minimal enclosing ball of conv{(t,…,t^d)} has center E and R²=S in odd dimension; in even d center E at a<=1, or λE (λ=(a²+1)/(2a²)) at a>1, with only two endpoint contacts except the even a>=1 regime where zero joins.
limitations: Requires symmetric interval and T containing both endpoints and 0, Euclidean metric in exact monomial coordinates.
